sources.author: Gertz, Bill
sources.title: Coronavirus link to China biowarfare program possible, analyst says
sources.summary: Washington Times article quoting analyst Dany Shoham on a possible link between the Wuhan outbreak and Chinese biological-warfare–related laboratories. Notes record an earlier 24 January headline variant tying Wuhan labs to a bio-warfare program.
sources.book_role: Introduces the early bioweapons hypothesis and Shoham’s analysis that Chapter 2 interrogates.

sources.author: Hoffman, David
sources.title: The Dead Hand: The Untold Story of the Cold War Arms Race and Its Dangerous Legacy
sources.summary: Amazon product page for David Hoffman’s history of Cold War nuclear/biological arms racing and the Soviet ‘Dead Hand’ legacy. Page is a retail landing page, not book text.
sources.book_role: Background reading on Cold War biological-weapons history informing Chapter 2’s bioweapons frame.

sources.author: Alibek, Ken, with Handelman, Stephen
sources.title: Biohazard: The Chilling True Story of the Largest Covert Biological Weapons Program in the World—Told from Inside by the Man Who Ran It
sources.summary: Amazon product page for Ken Alibek’s insider account of the Soviet biological weapons program. Retail landing page only.
sources.book_role: Key historical reference for covert state bioweapons programs discussed in Chapter 2.

sources.author: Branswell, Helen
sources.title: WHO says mysterious illness in China likely being caused by new virus
sources.summary: STAT report that WHO confirmed Chinese authorities believed a new coronavirus may cause Wuhan’s mysterious pneumonia cases, before China had fully stated that publicly.
sources.book_role: Tracks the early scientific/WHO framing of the outbreak as a novel coronavirus alongside bioweapons speculation.

sources.author: Rozo, Michelle, and Gigi Kwik Gronvall
sources.title: The reemergent 1977 H1N1 strain and the gain-of-function debate
sources.summary: mBio analysis linking the 1977 H1N1 reemergence (widely discussed as a possible lab-related event) to contemporary gain-of-function policy debates.
sources.book_role: Scientific precedent for lab-origin influenza used when Chapter 2 weighs accidental release vs bioweapon narratives.
